Hi Amit / Security team 

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps on the logging/redaction items we discussed: 

Summary of requirements we heard:
- PII redaction in request/response logs (card numbers, SSNs, customer emails)
- Masking or pseudonymization of trace IDs so debugging is possible but identifiers are not linkable to raw PII
- Ability to strip or allowlist headers (e.g., remove Authorization, Cookie headers from stored logs)
- Per-route/endpoint logging policies (sensitive payment flows vs. non-sensitive UI routes)
- Configurable retention windows (30/90/365 days) and the option to disable request/response logging for specific routes

Deliverables we've prepared and attached:
- redaction-spec-v1.pdf (draft mapping of PII patterns, header allowlist/blocklist, and example transformed logs)
- sample-logs-sanitized.txt (sanitized example showing before/after)

Proposed next steps:
1) Neha to share a technical summary and confirm whether Redwood can support per-route redaction + hashed trace IDs (see cc).
2) FintechCo to provide one sanitized sample payload or log snippet for us to validate transformation rules.
3) Schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive next week (we have Tue/Wed slots).

Amit  can you confirm which of the three items is highest priority for your team and whether Tuesday morning ET works for the deep-dive?

Thanks,

Thanks Marissa  appreciate the clear recap. A couple clarifications from the security/dev side: 

- We need trace IDs in error logs to correlate client incidents across services. We can accept pseudonymized trace IDs (hash + salt) but they must be stable enough for short-term debugging (24-48 hours) and not reversible.
- We still want request IDs (for performance tracing) to be available to our SREs but hashed; we do not want raw customer identifiers stored anywhere.
- Retention: default 90 days for most logs, but payment flows must be 30 days max.
- Header handling: Authorization and Cookie MUST be stripped. We might keep a small allowlist (User-Agent, X-Request-ID).

We can provide a sanitized example of a failing request payload by EOD Monday. Tue morning ET for a deep-dive works for us  propose 10:00 AM ET.

Also please include a technical owner from Redwood who can speak to the transform pipeline and HMAC options for hashing (cc if possible).

Best,
Amit
Security Engineering Lead, FintechCo
amit@fintechco.com

Hi Amit  looping in the technical folks and responding to the clarifications. Short answers up front and details below.

TL;DR: Yes, we can meet these requirements. We support per-route redaction rules, header allowlists, and deterministic pseudonymization for trace/request IDs (HMAC with customer-managed salt if required). We also support disabling request/response logging per route.

Details / Implementation options:
- Per-route policies: Redwood's runtime can tag routes and apply a transform pipeline at ingestion. That pipeline supports pattern matching for PII and header transformations.
- Header controls: configurable allowlist/blocklist configured in the Console or via API. Default templates strip Authorization, Cookie, and any header marked sensitive.
- Trace/Request IDs: two options:
  1) HMAC-based pseudonymization (recommended)  stable for the configured retention window, non-reversible without the key. We can offer KMS integration so you control the HMAC key.
  2) Short-lived mapping table  raw ID stored only in volatile memory for X hours for live debugging, then flushed.
- Redaction types supported: full redaction (REDACTED), masking (****-1234 for card numbers), hash/pseudonymization.
- Retention config: per-environment/per-route retention windows (30/90/365). Data export and deletion APIs available for audits.

Attachments: redaction-spec-v1.pdf contains pattern rules we propose. sample-logs-sanitized.txt shows examples: request headers before/after, response bodies with masked fields, and pseudonymized trace IDs.

Next steps we recommend:
1) You (FintechCo) send a sanitized failing request or log snippet (no PII) so we can validate rules against your payloads.
2) Schedule the 60-minute deep-dive (suggested agenda below). We can include a short demo of the Console redaction UI and the API calls to manage retention.

Suggested deep-dive agenda (60 min):
- 10 min: goals & prioritized flows (Amit)
- 20 min: demo of per-route redaction & header controls (Neha)
- 20 min: discussion of trace ID pseudonymization options and KMS/HSM key integration (Dev)
- 10 min: Q&A and next actions

Proposed attendees from Redwood: Neha Kapoor (Security Solutions), Dev Patel (Platform Eng), Marissa Cole (AE).

Please confirm meeting time (Marissa indicated Tue 10:00 AM ET).
